kicker: Microsoft AI's in-house image and voice

scenes.headline: How Microsoft swaps rented models for its own
scenes.sub: MAI-Image-2.5-Pro for quality, MAI-Voice-2-Flash for speed, both trained in-house.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Ziggy! Microsoft AI just put two of its own models into public preview, one for images and one for speech. Here's what they are, and where they went.

scenes.label: The move
scenes.text: Not a leaderboard win but a supply-chain move: build image and voice models in-house, then swap them in where outside models used to run.
scenes.mark: swap them in where outside models used to run
scenes.say: The idea isn't a leaderboard. It's a supply chain: train image and voice models in-house, then swap them in wherever an outside model used to run.

left.title: Rented
items: A third-party model behind the button
left.say: Rented, every image or utterance from a third-party API is marginal cost Microsoft doesn't control.

right.title: Owned
items: Trained in-house, on data it can trace
A Pro tier for quality, Flash for speed
right.say: Owned, it becomes an internal transfer. And each modality gets two lanes: a Pro tier for quality, a Flash tier for speed.

steps.say: Microsoft AI trains both itself. It says the image model learned from clean, traceable data, with no distillation from third-party models.

steps.note: PowerPoint: a claimed 84% lower GPU cost than GPT-Image-2
steps.say: The image model now runs all of Bing Image Creator, PowerPoint's image-to-image at a claimed eighty-four percent lower GPU cost, and OneDrive's default editor.
The voice model, a distilled sibling reported twice as fast, powers Dynamics 365 Contact Center at a claimed eighty-nine percent cost cut, and feeds Azure Voice Live.

scenes.title: Arena Elo gain over MAI-Image-2, by category
scenes.note: Microsoft's own tallies; no technical report was published
scenes.say: Where the image team pushed: legible text in the picture gained a hundred and seven Elo over the last generation. Microsoft's own tally, and there's no technical report.

scenes.text: The frontier being contested here isn't quality. It's who owns the model behind the button.
scenes.mark: who owns the model behind the button
scenes.say: So the frontier being contested isn't quality. It's who owns the model behind the button.

recap: Two in-house models: Pro for quality, Flash for speed
Swapped into Bing, Office and Dynamics 365
Every cost figure is Microsoft's own
scenes.say: To recap: two in-house models, two lanes, swapped in where rented ones used to run.
